It may slightly reduce background context for prior upper-airway symptoms but does not alter the emergency pathway here.

safety_verdicts.content: Shallow breathing / dyspnea on exertion since the sting
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript supports shallow breathing/dyspnea, but does not support 'dyspnea on exertion (DOE)'; DOE is an unsupported added detail.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Adding “dyspnea on exertion” (DOE) introduces an unsupported qualifier that can mischaracterize the dyspnea pattern and potentially confuse clinical interpretation (e.g., exertional/cardiac vs acute allergic respiratory compromise). In this case, dyspnea is still documented, so the patient would likely still be treated as urgent, limiting harm to potential miscommunication or minor downstream diagnostic drift.
